note: Law Nº 73/2018 of 31/08/2018 governing the credit reporting system (Official Gazette nº 37 of 10/09/2018), article 24(2): negative information on a person's credit history is kept and made available to users until five years from the final settlement of the amount in default, written as five; the law calls the keepers credit bureaus. Read on 2026-11-03 on the Rwanda Law Reform Commission's portal of laws. Until then the game held seven years, from Access Bank Rwanda's page ('until seven years after it is repaid'), which the law doesn't bear out; that page is no longer cited, and the bureau, named 'credit reference bureaus' after it, takes the law's name. The National Bank's Regulation 001/2015 and Regulation 27/2019 state no period. Whether Law 73/2018 has been amended since wasn't checked beyond the portal still listing it. No source read states how many days after its due date a missed payment is reported, so the days are the game's reading: the bureau's next monthly update.

sources.title: Law Nº 73/2018 of 31/08/2018 governing credit reporting system, Official Gazette nº 37 of 10/09/2018, article 24 (page 89), on the Portal of Rwandan Laws and Case Laws (Rwanda Law Reform Commission); the PDF is served from files.amategeko.gov.rw
sources.said: Article 24: Time limit for data conservation. Credit information is retained within the following time limit: 1° the credit report service provider retains and makes available to users positive information regarding data subject collected by credit bureaus for a period of five (5) years starting from the final date for payment. 2° negative information regarding data subject credit history is retained and made available to users until the expiry of a period of five (5) years from the date of final settlement of the amount in default. 3° credit bureaus make available positive and negative informations obtained from public sources to users for a period of five (5) years from the date of transmission or receipt of the information.
